title: introduce-phase-aware-latency-decomposer-and-compact-span-join
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a phase-aware invocation latency decomposer, compact span-log join helper, new dashboard panels for phase-percentile heatmaps, and tuned alerting rules to reduce long-tail noise.
description: Context: We get frequent noisy alerts driven by long-tail invocations where one phase (decode, kernel, or postprocess) dominates latency but is masked by aggregate p95/p99. Existing dashboards show overall latency distributions but not phase-level breakdowns correlated with payload shapes. Motivation: Provide a lightweight decomposition that attributes per-invocation latency into phases, bucket by payload size and model sequence length, and join compact span anchors to sampled logs without exploding cardinality. This enables: - Per-phase p50/p95/p99 heatmaps by payload-size buckets - Alert rules that can be scoped to phase regressions (e.g. kernel p95 increase) to reduce false positives - Compact log-span joins for investigations without full trace hydration Design summary: - Latency decomposer: new telemetry service module (telemetry/latency_decomposer.py) that subscribes to invocation spans and emits phase-attributed metrics with fixed buckets. Decomposer computes phase_durations: parse, encode, kv_cache, kernel, decode, postprocess. For memory and cardinality control we emit reservoir-summarized histograms and bounded label sets (payload_size_bucket, model_family, route). - Payload bucketing: bucketing based on payload token count and input_bytes with coarse bins (0-64,65-256,257-1024,1025+). - Compact span-join: a new span-join helper (svc/telemetry/compact_span_join.go) that produces a small fold of relevant logs (anchor_id, phase_timings_summary, error_flag) for sampled invocations. These join records are stored as low-cardinality tags rather than full log blobs. - Dashboard: new Grafana dashboard (dashboards/phase_latency_decomposer.json) with phase-wise heatmaps, cohort selection by payload bucket and model, and timeline comparison. - Alerting: prometheus alert_rules (infra/telemetry-prometheus/alert_rules.yaml) updated with: * phase_p95_increase_alert: looks at decomposed phase p95 deltas across rolling windows with adaptive thresholding * phase_noise_suppressor: a short-circuit that suppresses alerts when invocation cohort sizes < 100 in last 10m to reduce noisy signals Rollout plan: 1) Merge feature behind telemetry.feature_flags.phase_decomposer (off by default). 2) Canary: enable for 5% of traffic for 24h in us-west region and validate metric cardinality and CPU overhead. 3) Increase to 50% and monitor CPU/GPU serving overhead, metric cardinality, and alert volume. 4) Full rollout once thresholds met (see metrics below). Testing: - Unit tests for decomposition logic (tests/unit/test_latency_decomposer.py) - Integration test that runs synthetic invocations across payload buckets and asserts expected phase attributions (tests/integration/test_phase_decomposer.py) - Load bench: bench/decomposer_bench.py to estimate overhead. Observability/metrics produced: - telemetry.phase.duration_seconds{phase, payload_bucket, model_family, route} (histogram/reservoir) - telemetry.phase.duration_p{50,95,99}_by_payload (precomputed gauges for dashboard) - telemetry.compact_span.anchor_count and telemetry.compact_span.join_latency_ms Merge notes: squash merge; CI flaked once on integration test (timeout) and was rerun. Related work: builds on ENG-3920 (invocation sampling refactor) and complements pr-108246 (prefix warmup traces) for warmup signal. Security/opt-in: compact_span_join avoids logging user content; only emits aggregated timing and low-cardinality flags. Checklist: - [x] Decomposer module implemented - [x] Compact span join implemented - [x] Dashboard panels added - [x] Alert rules updated with noise suppressor - [x] Tests and bench added - [x] Feature flag gating implemented

summary: Introduce a bounded, phase-aware latency decomposition and compact span-log join that enables phase-level heatmaps and scoped alerting, reducing noisy long-tail alerts while keeping cardinality and storage bounded.
